caption: The drawing consists of six horizontal rectangular diagrams arranged vertically, each labeled with Roman numerals I through VI along the left margin. The topmost diagram (I) shows a simple rectangular grid drawn with thin black lines on a white background. The second diagram (II) is another rectangular grid, with certain squares filled in with small red dots forming the numbers “183” and the leftmost column highlighted with alternating red squares. The third diagram (III) fills the inside of the grid with a light blue color, leaving the "183" and its forming squares in alternating red and white, while the leftmost column remains highlighted with red and white. The fourth diagram (IV) uses round shapes instead of squares within the same grid; the majority of the circles are light blue, while the "183" formation and leftmost column are depicted with red circles containing smaller white circles at their centers. The fifth diagram (V) adds more intricacy, with blue and red interlocking circles of varying sizes, and more texture evident in the background, while still maintaining the "183" in red from the previous diagrams. The sixth and final diagram (VI) presents the most densely packed version, with full coverage of blue and red elements throughout, but the "183" remains discernible in red, surrounded by a dense blue background and a highlighted red left border. The artist’s signature, “C. Christeoffels”, appears in the bottom right corner. The primary colors used in the drawing are red, blue, and white.
title: Textile: Technique Demonstration
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
